writeup: TIC 43785616 is a candidate eclipsing binary star with an orbital period of 17.91 days, identified through automated analysis of TESS photometry. The system shows a primary eclipse with a dimming of 1.15%, detected with a signal-to-noise ratio of 160.8 in the BLS periodogram. Pixel-level image analysis confirms the signal at the target location with a peak signal-to-noise of 27.7, though the centroid offset of 6.7 arcseconds warrants continued attention. No secondary eclipse was detected. The target does not appear in six major variable-star catalogs, making it a novel candidate. However, alternating eclipses show significantly different depths, suggesting the true orbital period is double the initial measurement. This photometric signature, while not affecting the timing analysis, indicates caution is warranted in interpreting this candidate's properties.
